title: Elements of the state
competency: List the four elements of the state and explain why each is needed.

keywords.def: The people who live permanently on the territory of a state.
The area of land, with borders, where the people of a state live.
The operational arm of the state. It makes, enforces and interprets laws.
The supreme authority of a state inside and outside its borders.
The power of a state to command its own society.
The freedom of a state to deal with other countries without foreign control.

en.text: A state has four elements: population, territory, government and sovereignty. The people of a state do not have to share one race, religion, language or culture. No state can exist without a fixed territory with borders. The size of the population and territory is not fixed.

screens.title: Is Ethiopia a state?
opts: Yes, it has people, land, government and sovereignty
No, it has too many languages
Only Addis Ababa is a state
screens.after: Yes. Ethiopia has all four elements of a state. Many languages do not stop it being a state.

screens.title: 2.2 Elements of the state
paras: We identify a state by its fundamental elements.
They are population, territory, government and sovereignty.

screens.title: Population
paras: The population is an important element of the state.
The size of the population cannot be fixed.
The people do not have to be of a single race, religion, language or culture.
A modern state brings together the interests of different groups.
screens.note: Ethiopia's population is very diverse: many nations, nationalities and peoples (Figure 2.3).

screens.title: Territory
paras: No state can exist without a fixed territory.
People need territory to live and organize.
The size of the territory cannot be fixed. Vatican City is tiny; Russia covers 17,098,242 km².
Borders control the flow of people, money and goods.

screens.title: Key words
defs: The people who live permanently on the territory of a state.
The area of land, with borders, where the people of a state live.

screens.text: Which is NOT true about the population of a state?
opts: It must share one language and religion
screens.ans: It must share one language and religion
screens.why: The people of a state do not have to be of a single race, religion, language or culture.
Ethiopia is bordered by Eritrea (north), Djibouti (north-east), Somalia (east), Kenya (south), and South Sudan and Sudan (west).
screens.clue: Picture the map of the Horn of Africa.

screens.text: A state must have a large territory.
screens.why: The size of a territory cannot be fixed. Vatican City is very small but still a state.

screens.ask: No state can exist without a fixed ___.
screens.why: Territory is needed for people to live and organize.

screens.text: Chala says: "Ethiopia has more than 80 languages, so it cannot be one state." What is wrong?
opts: A state's people do not need one language or culture
screens.ans: A state's people do not need one language or culture
screens.why: The book says the people of a state do not have to be of a single race, religion, language or culture.
screens.clue: What does the book say about a state's people?

en.text: Government is an essential element of the state. There can be no state without government. Government is the operational arm of the state. It carries out state authority and makes, enforces and interprets laws.

screens.title: The two neighbours
screens.ask: Two neighbours argue about land. Elders try to help, but fail. Who should have the final say?
opts: The richest person in the village
screens.after: The government settles disputes by law, through courts. Read the case study below.

screens.title: Case study: The Two Neighbors!
paras: Two neighbours lived in the same village for a long time.
Over time they began to argue about land.
Each said the other had crossed the boundary.
Local elders tried to solve the problem. The neighbours did not accept their solution.

screens.title: Government
paras: Government is the third component of a state. There can be no state without government.
It is the operational arm of the state and a powerful political organization.
It carries out state authority and tasks.
It makes, enforces and interprets state laws.

screens.title: Key words
defs: The operational arm of the state. It makes, enforces and interprets laws.

screens.text: In the case study, who should give the final say?
screens.why: The state uses laws to settle disputes. The government gives citizens courts for this.
screens.clue: Who makes, enforces and interprets laws?

screens.text: What does the government do with state laws?
screens.why: The book says the government makes, enforces and interprets state laws.

screens.text: A state can exist without a government.
screens.why: There can be no state without government.
screens.clue: Read the first sentence about government.

screens.text: If a government stops doing its work, what is most likely to happen to schools?
opts: Students may not get a good education
screens.ans: Students may not get a good education
screens.why: Without a working government, there is no law and order and public services like schools fail.
screens.clue: Who provides public services like schools?

en.text: Sovereignty is the supreme authority of a state. Internal sovereignty is the power to command its own society. External sovereignty is the freedom to deal with other countries without foreign control. Ethiopia is a sovereign state with its own flag and national anthem. Its heroes defended its sovereignty, and it celebrates Victory Day.

screens.title: Who decides?
screens.ask: Another country tells Ethiopia whom to trade with. Ethiopia refuses. Which element of the state is Ethiopia protecting?
screens.after: Ethiopia is protecting its sovereignty: the freedom to decide its own relations with other countries.

screens.title: Sovereignty
paras: Sovereignty has two aspects: internal and external.
Internal sovereignty is the power to command its own society.
External sovereignty lets a state deal freely with other countries.
It is the supremacy of the state over all foreign wills.
screens.note: The book calls sovereignty the most vital and necessary component of the state.

screens.title: Ethiopia's sovereignty
paras: Ethiopia is a recognized sovereign state, with its own flag and national anthem.
Our ancestors sacrificed to protect it.
Ethiopian heroes defeated foreign invaders in many battles.
So Ethiopia kept its independence and celebrates Victory Day.

screens.title: Key words
defs: The supreme authority of a state inside and outside its borders.
The power of a state to command its own society.
The freedom of a state to deal with other countries without foreign control.

screens.text: What are the two aspects of sovereignty?
screens.why: Sovereignty has an internal and an external aspect.
screens.clue: Inside the country and outside it.

screens.title: Inside or outside?
items: Ethiopia makes laws for its own people
Ethiopia signs a trade deal with Kenya
The government keeps order in Ethiopian towns
screens.why: Internal = inside the state. External = relations with other states.
screens.clue: Is it about Ethiopia's own people, or about other countries?

screens.text: Ethiopia kept its independence because its heroes defeated foreign invaders.
screens.why: Ethiopian heroes defeated foreign invaders, so Ethiopia kept its independence.

opts: Can Ethiopia choose its friends abroad without foreign orders?
Can the police keep order in Adama?
screens.ans: Can Ethiopia choose its friends abroad without foreign orders?
screens.why: External sovereignty is about independent relations with other countries.
screens.clue: External means the relation with other states.

opts: Yes, it has population, territory, government and sovereignty
No, it has too many peoples
Yes, because it has big cities
items.ans: Yes, it has population, territory, government and sovereignty

items.text: Which country borders Ethiopia to the south?
Which countries border Ethiopia on the west?
items.why: South Sudan and Sudan are on the west.

items.text: If the neighbours cannot solve the dispute themselves or with elders, what should they do?
opts: Take it to the government or a court
items.ans: Take it to the government or a court
items.why: The state settles disputes by law, through courts.

items.text: In a democratic state, who makes, enforces and interprets laws?
items.why: The government makes, enforces and interprets state laws.

items.text: Why is a state's sovereignty important?
opts: It lets the state command its society and deal freely with other states
It gives every citizen a car
It removes the need for laws
items.ans: It lets the state command its society and deal freely with other states
items.why: Internal sovereignty commands its society; external sovereignty gives independent relations.

test.text: How many essential elements does a state have?
There can be no state without government.
Which element is the supreme authority of the state inside and outside?
The people of a state must speak one language.
test.why: The people do not have to share one race, religion, language or culture.

test.text: A country makes its own laws but a foreign power controls its trade with others. Which aspect is missing?
test.why: External sovereignty is freedom in relations with other countries.

notes.text: The book says Vatican City covers 110 hectares; it is about 44 hectares (about 110 acres). The lesson does not use the number. Teacher to confirm.
The book calls government "the third and most important component" (p.42) and sovereignty "the most vital and necessary component" (p.43). The lesson treats all four elements as essential.
"scarification of our forefathers" (p.44) is read as "sacrifice".
Figure 2.2 says "People" where the text says "Population"; the lesson uses Population.
Open check-points (diversity of Ethiopia, flag colours, national anthem, naming heroes, duties of youth) are not graded: their answers are not in the book.
